title: The rest of the five
hookLine: Dharam Singh survived the Guru; Himmat, Mohkam and Sahib Singh fell at Chamkaur

cards: Team photos shrink in memory. Years later, people remember the captain, the one who scored, the one who gave the speech. The rest blur into the back row.
The Panj Pyare could easily have gone that way: one well-known first volunteer, then four others who followed. But Sikhs don't let them blur. They say all five names.
They tell where each one came from and how each one's life ended. So today, after the man who stood first, the rest of the five.

teach.b: Dharam Singh, Himmat Singh, Mohkam Singh, Sahib Singh. Tradition says they came from far-flung places and different trades: a farmer, a water-carrier, a washerman, a barber.

Men who, in the world around them, would not have eaten at one table. On the day the Khalsa began, each rose after Daya Ram and walked into the tent, one at a time. After that day, their lives went in two directions.

Bhai Dharam Singh lived on. Tradition says he stayed with the Guru through the worst of what came, and was still at his side when the Guru traveled south, near the end of his life. He outlived the Guru.

The other three did not. When the Guru's small band was surrounded at Chamkaur, Himmat Singh, Mohkam Singh and Sahib Singh were among the Sikhs inside the mud walls. Tradition says they went out to fight, and fell there.
Three of the five beloved gave their lives in one place.

Some of the five are remembered for how they lived on and kept serving, some for how they died. The tradition doesn't rank them. It puts them side by side, the way they stood when they came out of the tent.
The Sikh prayer called Ardas, said at the end of gatherings and daily prayers, remembers the five beloved. And at every amrit ceremony, five Sikhs stand in their place to prepare the amrit.
The five keep coming back, as five. Remembering someone by name is a small thing. But it is how the back row gets out of the blur.

how: Sikhs remember the Panj Pyare in Ardas, and at an amrit ceremony five initiated Sikhs serve as the Panj Pyare to prepare and give the amrit.

games.why: Sikhs name all five, and keep them together, as they stood coming out of the tent.

practice: Say the five names slowly, one to each long breath: Daya Singh, Dharam Singh, Himmat Singh, Mohkam Singh, Sahib Singh.
Then, if you like, add your own back row, the people who quietly made things possible and never got the credit, one name to each breath.

wordCard.voice: Panj Pyare. The five beloved: Daya Singh, Dharam Singh, Himmat Singh, Mohkam Singh and Sahib Singh, the first members of the Khalsa. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: Panj Pyare, the five beloved.

carryVoice: Your line: the five, remembered. At every amrit, five still stand together. That's day eight hundred twenty-two.
